<style type="text/css">
html {
   overflow-y: scroll;
}

body {
   padding: 0;
   margin: 0;
   -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
   font: 13px/1.231 arial, helvetica, clean, sans-serif;
}

body.warn-page {
   background: #ffffcc;
}

#page-container {
   margin: 0;
   padding: 0;
   min-width: 1275px;
}

.kdp-top-header {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindlepubs/common/layouts/nav-bar-bg._V156427298_.png")
      repeat-x scroll 0 0 transparent;
   height: 29px;
}

.header-row {
   background-color: #F5F5F5;
   padding-top: 6px;
   padding-bottom: 3px;
}

.top-links {
   padding: 5px 20px;
   text-align: right;
}

.top-links a, .top-links .language-chooser, .header-item, .header-item .language-chooser {
   margin: 0 10px;
}

.kdp-delim {
   color: #CCCCCC;
}

.language-option {
   font-size: 11px;
}

.language-option a {
   margin: 5px;
}

.language-option .disable {
   color: #666666;
   margin: 0 5px;
}

body .kdp-header {
   color: #004B91;
   height: 95px;
   padding: 35px 0 0 0;
   position: relative;
   text-align: left;
}

.a-lt-ie8 body .kdp-header {
   height: 90px;
}

.tabs {
   color: #004B91;
   font-family: Arial;
   text-decoration: none;
}

.kdp-header .tabs {
   font-size: 16px;
}

.kdp-header .tabs .kdp-delim {
   padding: 0 15px;
}

.kdp-header .tabs .selected {
   font-weight: bold;
}

.account-incomplete {
   margin-top: 1em;
   position: absolute;
   right: 0;
   top: 0;
}

.account-incomplete .a-alert-content {
   font-size: 13px;
   color: #333;
}

.kdp-top-footer {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindlepubs/common/layouts/footer-top._V192549182_.gif")
      repeat-x scroll 0 0 transparent;
   height: 23px;
   margin-top: 1em;
}

.social-footer {
   color: #666666;
   text-align: left;
}

.kdp-footer {
   color: #666666;
   text-align: left;
   font-family: Verdana, Geneva, Sans-Serif;
   font-size: 10px;
   margin: 20px 0;
   padding: 0 10px;
   position: relative;
}

.social-footer .links a, .kdp-footer .links a {
   color: #666666;
   text-decoration: underline;
}

.social-footer .links, .kdp-footer .links {
   text-align: center;
}

.kdp-footer .cr, .kdp-footer .kdp-social, .kdp-footer .links {
   padding-top: 10px;
}

.kdp-social a {
   display: inline-block;
}

.kdp-facebook {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/find-us-on-facebook-intl._V142003952_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 0 transparent;
   cursor: pointer;
   height: 20px;
   margin-right: 10px;
   width: 75px;
}

.en_US .kdp-facebook {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/find-us-on-facebook-a._V151334219_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 0 transparent;
}

.ja_JP .kdp-facebook {
   background: url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/jp/sprite-kdp-jp._V135734257_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 -2820px transparent;
   height: 22px;
   margin-right: 15px;
   width: 73px;
}

.kdp-twitter {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/follow-us-on-x-intl._V1736794651_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 0 transparent;
   cursor: pointer;
   height: 20px;
   width: 73px;
}

.en_US .kdp-twitter {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/follow-us-on-x-a._V1736794567_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 0 transparent;
}

.ja_JP .kdp-twitter {
   background: url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/jp/sprite-kdp-jp._V135734257_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 -2861px transparent;
   height: 22px;
   width: 78px;
}

.kdp-instagram {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/follow-us-on-instagram-intl._V1736453912_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 0 transparent;
   cursor: pointer;
   height: 20px;
   width: 82px;
}

.en_US .kdp-instagram {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/follow-us-on-instagram-a._V1736454729_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 0 transparent;
}

.social-footer .kdp-facebook {
   width: 20px;
   margin-right: 5px;
}

.social-footer .kdp-twitter {
   width: 30px;
}

.social-footer .kdp-instagram {
   width: 30px;
}

p.agreements-instructions {
   margin: 0 0 7px 5px;
}

.kdp-header .kdp-header-text {
   font-size: 28px;
   font-weight: normal;
   color: black;
   line-height: 1.2;
   text-align: center;
}

a:link.footer-link, a:visited.footer-link  {
   font-family: arial, sans-serif;
   color: rgb(153, 153, 153);
   text-decoration: none;
   line-height: 11px;
   font-size: 10px;
   display: block;

            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Paperback Submission Guidelines
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               These guidelines are for <b>designers</b> of paperbacks with full-color covers, with any interior type.

<p>For help formatting your paperback manuscript, see our guides for <a href="/help?topicId=G202145400">Microsoft Word for Windows</a>, <a href="/help?topicId=GLRF8JDXY5LPE3TX">Microsoft Word for Mac</a> and <a href="/help?topicId=G3TQWMMGK8528NDZ">Pages for Mac</a>. You can also try our <a href="https://www.amazon.com/Kindle-Create/b?ie=UTF8&node=18292298011">Kindle Create</a> tool to format your paperback interiors.</p>

<div class="a-span4">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<h3>Contents</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="#limit">New title creation and submission limits</a></li>
<li><a href="#fileguide">File guidelines</a></li>
<li><a href="#coverspec">Cover specifications</a>
	<ul>
	<li><a href="#covercalc">Calculating cover size</a></li>
	<li><a href="#coverformat">Cover formatting</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinebw">Spine measurements for black and white books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinegw">Spine measurements for groundwood books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinecolor">Spine measurements for color books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinetext">Spine text</a></li>
	<li><a href="#barcode">Barcodes</a></li>
	</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="#intspec">Interior specifications</a></li>
</ul>
</div>

<hr>

<h3 id="limit">New title creation and submission limits</h3>
<p>To help promote a positive experience for all authors and readers, we limit how many new titles per format you can create and how many you can submit for publication each week. Both limits apply separately to each book format and reset every Sunday at 12:00 AM Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). For full details, visit <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G202172740">Create a Book</a>.

</p><hr>

<h3 id="fileguide">File guidelines</h3>

<h4 id="filems">Manuscript</h4>
<ul>
<li><b>Bleed:</b> If your book has images or elements that bleed to the edges of your pages, you must upload your manuscript as a PDF.</li>
<li><b>No Bleed:</b> If your book does not contain bleed, you can upload your manuscript as a PDF, DOC, DOCX, RTF, HTML, or TXT file. KDP will automatically convert these file types to PDF prior to publishing/printing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="filecover">Cover</h4>
<p>You can create your book cover using KDP's <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G201113520">Cover Creator</a> tool or submit your book cover in a PDF. (Cover Creator accepts JPG, PNG, and GIF file formats.)</p>

<h4 id="filespec">File specifications</h4>
<ul>
<li>Ensure file size is not more than 650MB.</li>
<li>File names for cover and interior files must not contain emoji characters or other unsupported special characters.</li>
<li>Embed all fonts and images in your native file prior to submission.</li>
<li>Flatten transparent objects and layers in the native file before publishing.</li>
<li>Submitted files should not contain crop marks, trim marks, bookmarks, comments, invisible objects, annotations, placeholder text, or metadata.</li>
<li>All images (both cover and manuscript) should be at least 300 DPI.</li>
<li>Optimize PDFs. Optimization is useful to reduce your file size, allowing for higher performance when transferring, uploading, viewing, and printing the files.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="filefail">Common points of failure</h4>
<ul>
<li>Not flattening transparent objects and/or layers in the native file</li>
<li>Locked or encrypted files</li>
<li>File names containing emoji or unsupported special characters</li>
<li>Files with crop marks, trim marks, bookmarks, comments, invisible objects, annotations, placeholder text, or metadata</li>
<li>Missing pages</li>
<li>Excessive blank pages</li>
<li>Title missing on the front cover</li>
<li>Barcode missing</li>
<li>Incorrect pagination</li>
<li>PDF creation logos or watermarks</li>
</ul>

<hr>

<h3 id="coverspec">Cover specifications</h3>

<h4 id="covercalc">Calculating cover size</h4>
<p>To format your paperback cover, you'll first need to calculate the spine measurements (<a href="#spinebw">black and white books</a>, <a href="#spinegw">groundwood books</a>, <a href="#spinecolor">color books</a>).</p>
<p>Insert the spine measurements, selected trim size width and height, and the 0.125" (3.2 mm) bleed requirement into the following equations to find your cover size:</p>
<ul>
<li>Cover Width = Bleed + Back Cover Width + Spine Width + Front Cover Width + Bleed</li>
<li>Cover Height = Bleed + Trim Height + Bleed</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="coverformat">Cover formatting</h4>
<ul>
<li>Covers should be one continuous image centered left to right on the spine.</li>
<li>Flatten all layers in the native file.</li>
<li>Bleed of 0.125" (3.2 mm) is required on all sides. Bleed at the bottom of the page cannot exceed 0.125" (3.2 mm).</li>
<li>Any content you don't intend to be trimmed off should be a minimum of 0.25" (6.4 mm) from the outside cover edge.</li>
<li>Embed all fonts on the cover in the native program before publishing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinebw">Spine measurements for black and white books</h4>
<ul>
<li>White paper: page count x 0.002252" (0.0572 mm)</li>
<li>Cream paper: page count x 0.0025" (0.0635 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinegw">Spine measurements for groundwood books</h4>
<ul>
<li>Groundwood paper: page count x 0.00235" (0.0596 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinecolor">Spine measurements for color books</h4>
<ul>
<li>Color paper: page count x 0.002347" (0.0596 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinetext">Spine text</h4>
<p>We only print spine text on books with more than 79 pages. Text on larger spines must be sized to fit the spine, with at least 0.0625" (1.6 mm) of space between the text and the edge of the spine. Every book varies slightly when bound. Allow for 0.0625" (1.6 mm) variance on either side of the fold lines for your cover.</p>

<h4 id="barcode">Barcodes</h4>
<p>You can upload a cover with or without a barcode. If you choose not to provide your own barcode, we'll automatically place one on your back cover. Learn more about <a href="/help?topicId=G5HDYGP4BXLX4RUW">barcodes</a>.</p>

<hr>

<h3 id="intspec">Interior specifications</h3>

<h4 id="pagespread">Page spreads</h4>
<p>We require single page files (as opposed to spreads or 2-up files).</p>

<h4 id="pagesize">Page size</h4>

<h5 id="nobleed">No bleed</h5>
<p>Set the page size to your selected trim size (width by height).</p>

<h5 id="bleed">Interior full bleed</h5>
<ul>
<li>If you want your images to bleed to the edges of your pages, extend them 0.125" (3.2 mm) beyond the final trim size from the top, bottom, and outer edges of your manuscript.</li>
<li>Format your PDF manuscript at 0.25" (6.4 mm) higher and 0.125" (3.2 mm) wider than your selected trim size in order to print the full bleed area.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="font">Font</h4>
<ul>
<li>Minimum font size: 7 points</li>
<li>All fonts in the interior files should be embedded in the native program before publishing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="imgres">Image resolution</h4>
<p>Minimum resolution of 300 DPI. There is no set maximum DPI for images, however, images with excessively high resolutions may result in files timing out during processing, or may cause manufacturing delays. We recommend a maximum resolution of 600 DPI, to keep your total file size under 650MB.</p>

<h4 id="pag">Pagination</h4>
<ul>
<li>Order all page numbers sequentially, with even numbers on left pages and odd numbers on the right for the left to right content, and with even numbers on right pages and odd numbers on the left for the right to left content.</li>
<li>You can use Roman numerals to indicate the beginning of the manuscript, and then continue with standard page numbering.</li>
<li>You may continue page numbering from a previous book in a subsequent volume of a series as long as the series name and volume number are clearly labeled.</li>
<li>We allow scanned content with sequential original page numbering clearly visible in the footer of the manuscript file.</li>
</ul>

         <div class="a-section a-spacing-large">
            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Paperback Printing Cost
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               KDP prints your book on demand and subtracts your printing costs from your royalties. That means you don't have to pay any costs upfront or carry any inventory.
<br><br>
<b>Note:</b> <a href="https://www.amazon.com.br">amazon.com.br</a>, <a href="https://www.amazon.com.in">amazon.com.in</a>, and <a href="https://www.amazon.com.mx">amazon.com.mx</a> do not support paperback and hardcover distribution.
<br><br>
<hr>
<h3>Contents</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="#calculate">How we calculate printing cost</a></li>

<hr>
<a name="calculate"></a>
<h3>
How we calculate printing cost
</h3>
Printing costs vary depending on trim size, page count, ink type (black ink or color ink), and paper type. Bleed settings and cover finish don't affect printing cost. Printing cost also depends on which Amazon marketplace (website) a reader ordered your book from. Based on the <a href="/help?topicId=G201834180">print options</a> you choose, KDP calculates and displays your printing cost in the Rights & Pricing section of your title setup.
<br><br>
To calculate your paperback's printing cost, we use this formula:
<br><br>
<b>Fixed cost + (page count * per page cost) = printing cost</b>
<br><br>
To estimate your printing cost, use KDP's <a href="/royalty-calculator">Printing Cost & Royalty Calculator</a>.
<br><br>
The charts below summarize printing cost calculations by marketplace where the book is sold.

<a name="calculation"></a>
<h3>
Printing cost calculation examples
</h3>
<b>Black ink, regular trim size</b>
<br>
Example #1: 300-page black ink regular trim size paperback sold in the United States:<br>
Based on the <a href="#blackink">black ink</a> chart above, the fixed cost for a 300-page black ink regular trim size paperback sold on Amazon.com is 1.00 USD, and the additional cost per page is 0.012 USD.
<br><br>
1.00 USD fixed cost + (300 page count * 0.012 USD per page cost) = 4.60 USD (printing cost)
<br><br>
Example #2: 55-page black ink regular trim size paperback sold in the United Kingdom:<br>
Fixed cost for a 55-page black ink regular trim size paperback sold on Amazon.co.uk is 1.93 GBP, and the additional cost per page is 0.00 GBP (none).
<br><br>
1.93 GBP fixed cost + (55 page count * 0.00 GBP per page cost ) = 1.93 GBP (printing cost)
<br><br>
<b>Standard color ink, regular trim size</b>
<br>
Example #1: 150-page standard color ink regular trim size paperback sold in Germany:<br>
Based on the <a href="#colorink">color ink</a> chart above, the fixed cost for a 150-page standard color ink regular trim size paperback sold on Amazon.de is 0.75 EUR, and the additional cost per page is 0.024 EUR.
<br><br>
0.75 EUR fixed cost + (150 page count * 0.024 EUR per page cost) = 4.35 EUR (printing cost)
<br><br>
Example #2: 600-page standard color ink regular trim size paperback sold in Canada: <br>
Based on the <a href="#colorink">color ink</a> chart above, the fixed cost for a 600-page standard color ink regular trim size paperback sold on Amazon.ca is 1.26 CAD, and the additional cost per page is 0.037 CAD.
<br><br>
1.26 CAD fixed cost + (600 page count * 0.037 CAD per page cost ) =  23.46 CAD (printing cost)
<br><br>
<b>Premium color ink, large trim size</b>
<br>
Example #1: 50-page premium color ink large trim size paperback sold in Australia:<br>
Based on the <a href="#colorink">color ink</a> chart above, the fixed cost for a 50-page premium color ink large trim size paperback sold on Amazon.com.au is 2.42 AUD, and the additional cost per page is 0.10 AUD.
<br><br>
2.42 AUD fixed cost + (50 page count * 0.10 AUD per page cost) = 7.42 AUD (printing cost)
<br><br>

<a name="min"></a>
<h3>Minimum paperback list price</h3>
The minimum list price is calculated based on your book's printing cost and royalty rate. It ensures that your royalties earned are always enough to cover the cost to print your book. KDP will not allow you to enter a list price lower than the minimum list price.
<br><br>
To calculate your minimum list price, we divide your paperback's printing cost by the royalty rate (50% or 60%, depending upon list price, per marketplace – please check the <a href="/help?topicId=G202181110">Royalties help page</a>).
<br><br>
<p>Scenario 1: Your book's list price is in the 60% royalty range:</p>
<b>Printing cost / (60 / 100) royalty rate = minimum list price</b><p></p>
<p>Scenario 2: Your book's list price is in the 50% royalty range:</p>
<p><b>Printing cost / (50 / 100) royalty rate = minimum list price</b></p>
<br><br>

<style type="text/css">
html {
   overflow-y: scroll;
}

body {
   padding: 0;
   margin: 0;
   -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
   font: 13px/1.231 arial, helvetica, clean, sans-serif;
}

body.warn-page {
   background: #ffffcc;
}

#page-container {
   margin: 0;
   padding: 0;
   min-width: 1275px;
}

.kdp-top-header {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindlepubs/common/layouts/nav-bar-bg._V156427298_.png")
      repeat-x scroll 0 0 transparent;
   height: 29px;
}

.header-row {
   background-color: #F5F5F5;
   padding-top: 6px;
   padding-bottom: 3px;
}

.top-links {
   padding: 5px 20px;
   text-align: right;
}

.top-links a, .top-links .language-chooser, .header-item, .header-item .language-chooser {
   margin: 0 10px;
}

.kdp-delim {
   color: #CCCCCC;
}

.language-option {
   font-size: 11px;
}

.language-option a {
   margin: 5px;
}

.language-option .disable {
   color: #666666;
   margin: 0 5px;
}

body .kdp-header {
   color: #004B91;
   height: 95px;
   padding: 35px 0 0 0;
   position: relative;
   text-align: left;
}

.a-lt-ie8 body .kdp-header {
   height: 90px;
}

.tabs {
   color: #004B91;
   font-family: Arial;
   text-decoration: none;
}

.kdp-header .tabs {
   font-size: 16px;
}

.kdp-header .tabs .kdp-delim {
   padding: 0 15px;
}

.kdp-header .tabs .selected {
   font-weight: bold;
}

.account-incomplete {
   margin-top: 1em;
   position: absolute;
   right: 0;
   top: 0;
}

.account-incomplete .a-alert-content {
   font-size: 13px;
   color: #333;
}

.kdp-top-footer {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindlepubs/common/layouts/footer-top._V192549182_.gif")
      repeat-x scroll 0 0 transparent;
   height: 23px;
   margin-top: 1em;
}

.social-footer {
   color: #666666;
   text-align: left;
}

.kdp-footer {
   color: #666666;
   text-align: left;
   font-family: Verdana, Geneva, Sans-Serif;
   font-size: 10px;
   margin: 20px 0;
   padding: 0 10px;
   position: relative;
}

.social-footer .links a, .kdp-footer .links a {
   color: #666666;
   text-decoration: underline;
}

.social-footer .links, .kdp-footer .links {
   text-align: center;
}

.kdp-footer .cr, .kdp-footer .kdp-social, .kdp-footer .links {
   padding-top: 10px;
}

.kdp-social a {
   display: inline-block;
}

.kdp-facebook {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/find-us-on-facebook-intl._V142003952_.png")
      no-repeat scroll 0 0 transparent;
   cursor: pointer;
   height: 20px;
   margin-right: 10px;

            <a id="help-topic-crumb-GGE5T76TWKA85DJM" class="a-link-normal" href="/en_US/help/topic/GGE5T76TWKA85DJM">Low-Content Books</a>

         <div class="a-section a-spacing-large">
            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Low-Content Books
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               <p>A low-content book has minimal or no content on the interior pages. Low-content books are generally repetitive, and designed to be filled in by the user. This does not typically include activity books, such as puzzle books or coloring books, which generally do not feature repetitive content on each page. See common examples of low-content books in the table below, but note that there can be exceptions.</p>

<p>Low-content books do not require an ISBN. If you want an ISBN for your low-content book, you can use your own ISBN, or publish without an ISBN. Low-content books are not eligible for the free KDP ISBN. See the differences between using your own ISBN and publishing without an ISBN below.</p>

<b>Note:</b> we don't currently offer Release Date for low-content books.
<br><br>

<div class="a-span4">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<h3>Contents</h3>
<hr>
<li><a href="#examples">Examples of low-content books</a></li>
<li><a href="#howto">How to create a low-content book</a></li>
<li><a href="#barcode">What type of barcode will appear on a low-content book?</a></li>
<li><a href="#updates">What information can be updated after publishing a low-content book?</a></li>
<li><a href="#changeISBN">Changing your ISBN option</a></li>
<li><a href="#differences">Differences between using your own ISBN and publishing without an ISBN</a></li>
</div></div></div>

<br>
<hr>

<a name="examples"></a>
<h3>Examples of low-content books</h3>
<br>
<table cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" border="1">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Low-Content</th>
<th>Not Generally Low-Content</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Notebooks</td><td>Novels</td></tr>
<tr><td>Planners</td><td>Nonfiction</td></tr>
<tr><td>Diaries/Journals</td><td>Puzzle books</td></tr>
<tr><td>Prompt journals</td><td>Coloring books</td></tr>
<tr><td>Log books (i.e., tracking habits, activity, thankfulness)</td><td>Photography</td></tr>
<tr><td>Coupon books</td><td>Sheet music</td></tr>
<tr><td>Score card templates</td><td>Manuals</td></tr>
<tr><td>Crafting templates (i.e., scrapbook paper, ephemera books, etc.)</td><td>Textbooks</td></tr>
<tr><td>Blank sheet music (also known as manuscript or staff paper)</td><td>Children's books</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<br>
Note: there can be exceptions to these examples.
<br><br>

<hr>

<a name="howto"></a>
<h3>How to create a low-content book</h3>

Creating a low-content book is similar to creating other print books, but your ISBN options are different as noted in the steps below. To publish a low-content book:
<br><br>

<ol>
<li>Go to your <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/bookshelf">Bookshelf</a>.</li>
<li>Click <b>+ Create new title or series</b> and then select <b>Create paperback</b> or <b>Create hardcover</b>.</li>
<li>Enter your information for each section as follows:
<ul>
<li><b>Paperback or Hardcover details.</b> Enter your title, description, keywords, etc. Under <b>Categories</b> you need to check the <b>Low-content</b> box. Please note that if you do not select this box, or select a different box, your book will be rejected.</li>
<li><b>Paperback or Hardcover content.</b> Under <b>Print ISBN</b>, you can choose between <b>Publish without an ISBN</b> or <b>Use my own ISBN</b>. Upload your manuscript and cover files, preview your book, and order a proof.</li>
<li><b>Paperback or Hardcover rights and pricing.</b> Choose the territories where you hold distribution rights and set your list price.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>After entering your information, click <b>Publish Your Paperback Book</b> or <b>Publish Your Hardcover Book.</b></li>
</ol>

See more detailed instructions on <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G202172740">creating a book</a>.
<br><br><p>Hardcover publishing is not supported on kdp.amazon.co.jp. </p>

<hr>

<a name="barcode"></a>
<h3>What type of barcode will appear on a low-content book?</h3>

If you use your own ISBN, you can upload a cover with or without a barcode. If you choose the option <b>Publish without an ISBN</b>, or decide not to provide your own barcode, we'll automatically place one on your back cover.
<br><br>
We'll place a barcode in a 2" (50.8 mm) by 1.2" (30.5 mm) white box in the lower right-hand corner of your book's back cover. If you leave images or text on this part of the cover, the barcode will cover them during printing, which could result in your file being rejected, so don't include any text or objects in this area.
<br><br>
Low-content books that are published without an ISBN are not eligible for Transparency codes. <b>Note:</b> Transparency codes are being retired from KDP print barcodes and are not available for books created after November 2025.
<br><br>
Learn more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G5HDYGP4BXLX4RUW">barcodes</a>.
<br><br>

<hr>

<a name="updates"></a>
<h3>What information can be updated after publishing a low-content book?</h3>

After publishing your book, certain features are locked. Learn more about the <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G200736410#can_update_after_publishing">changes that can be made after publishing</a>.
<br><br>

<hr>

<a name="changeISBN"></a>
<h3>Changing your ISBN option</h3>

You cannot change your ISBN selection after you've published your book.
<br><br>
If you need to change your ISBN selection after publishing your book, you'll need to unpublish your book from your KDP Bookshelf, and then republish it. See more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G4QJH4ENN4FZRFMP">unpublishing a book</a>.
<br><br>

<hr>

<a name="differences"></a>
<h3>Differences between using your own ISBN and publishing without an ISBN</h3>

There are a few differences regarding supported features if you decide to use your own ISBN or publish your low-content book without one, which we've included in the below table.
<br><br>

<table cellpadding="10" border="1">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><b>Expanded Distribution</b></td>
<td>Expanded Distribution is not supported for low-content books, regardless of the ISBN option you select. Learn more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/GQTT4W3T5AYK7L45#eligibility">enrollment requirements</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><b>Read Sample (Look Inside the Book) feature</b></td>
<td>The sample and the back cover thumbnail are currently not supported for low-content books published without ISBN. If you'd like to activate this feature for your book, we recommend you to buy your own ISBN from Bowker or through your local ISBN agency. Learn more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G201834170#Howto_own_ISBN">using your own ISBN</a>.
<br><br>
Alternatively, you can use A+ Content to add images of your book's interior so buyers can see what it looks like. These images will appear on your book detail page. Learn more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/GHL7P99B7AA543CN">A+ Content</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><b>Series</b></td>
<td>Low-content books are not eligible for creating a series, regardless of the ISBN option you select. Learn more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/GMFKBUS43QQ5AJ5A">series</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><b>Transparency codes</b></td>
<td>Low-content books that are published without an ISBN are not eligible for Transparency codes. <b>Note:</b> Transparency codes are being retired from KDP print barcodes and are not available for books created after November 2025. Learn more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G5HDYGP4BXLX4RUW">barcodes</a>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Content Guidelines
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               <p><br></p><!--<h2>Content Guidelines</h2>-->
<!--https://ajuda.a2z.com/cms.html?repo=GQRG9D4WWKTRVGY2&object=G200672390-->
<!--https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G200672390-->
As a bookseller, we believe that providing access to the written word is important, including content that may be considered objectionable. We carefully consider the types of content we make available in our stores and review our approach regularly, listening to feedback and investigating concerns from our customers. We reserve the right to remove content from sale if we determine it creates a poor customer experience.
<br><br>
Authors, publishers, and selling partners are responsible for adhering to our content guidelines. We invest significant time and resources to enforce these guidelines, using a combination of machine learning, automation, and dedicated teams of human reviewers. We’ll reject or remove content that does not adhere to these guidelines and promptly investigate any book when notified of potential noncompliance.  We may also request additional information relating to your book before it's available for sale. If we remove a title, we let the author, publisher, or selling partner know and they can appeal our decision.
<br><br>
These guidelines apply to book content, including title, cover art, and product description. 
<br><br>
<b>Note:</b> Books that are translations of another work must credit the translator and the original author in the contributor field. If the work is not a new translation and the translator is unknown, the publisher should list the translator as "Anonymous" in the contributor field.
<br><br>
<h3>Contents</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="#illegal">Illegal or infringing content</a></li>
	<li><a href="#offensive">Offensive content</a></li>
	<li><a href="#aicontent">Artificial intelligence (AI) content</a></li>
	<li><a href="#customerexperience">Poor customer experience</a></li>
<li><a href="#publicdomain">Public domain content</a></li>
<li><a href="#Score and lyrics">Score and lyrics for songs managed by copyright management companies (Japan Only)</a></li>
	<li><a href="#report">Report violations</a></li>
</ul>
<hr>
	<a name="illegal"></a>
<h3>Illegal or infringing content</h3>
We take violations of laws and proprietary rights very seriously. It is the responsibility of authors, publishers, and selling partners to ensure their content doesn't violate laws or copyright, trademark, brand, privacy, publicity, or other rights. We will not accept content under copyright that is freely available on the web unless it’s provided by the owner of the copyright. In addition, we do not allow companion books based on copyrighted works (e.g., summaries, study guides, etc.) to be published outside the U.S. without written permission from the copyright holder.
<br><br>
<hr>
	<a name="offensive"></a>
<h3>Offensive content</h3>
We don’t sell certain content including content that we determine is hate speech, promotes the abuse or sexual exploitation of children, contains pornography, glorifies rape or pedophilia, advocates terrorism, or other material we deem inappropriate or offensive.
<br><br>
<hr>
	<a name="aicontent"></a>
<h3>Artificial intelligence (AI) content (text, images, or translations)</h3>
We require you to inform us of AI-generated content (text, images, or translations) when you publish a new book or make edits to and republish an existing book through KDP. AI-generated images include cover and interior images and artwork. You are not required to disclose AI-assisted content. We distinguish between <b>AI-generated</b> and <b>AI-assisted</b> content as follows:
<br><br>
<ul>
<li><b>AI-generated</b>: We define AI-generated content as text, images, or translations created by an AI-based tool. If you used an AI-based tool to create the actual content (whether text, images, or translations), it is considered "AI-generated," even if you applied substantial edits afterwards. 
</li>
	<li><b>AI-assisted</b>: If you created the content yourself, and used AI-based tools to edit, refine, error-check, or otherwise improve that content (whether text or images), then it is considered "AI-assisted" and not “AI-generated.” Similarly, if you used an AI-based tool to brainstorm and generate ideas, but ultimately created the text or images yourself, this is also considered "AI-assisted" and not “AI-generated.” It is not necessary to inform us of the use of such tools or processes.</li>
</ul>
<p>You are responsible for verifying that all AI-generated and/or AI-assisted content adheres to all content guidelines, including by complying with all applicable intellectual property rights.</p>
<hr>
	<a name="customerexperience"></a>
<h3>Poor customer experience</h3>
Books for sale on Amazon should provide a positive customer experience. We do not allow descriptive content meant to mislead customers or that doesn't accurately represent the content of the book. We also do not allow content that’s typically disappointing to customers, including the examples provided in the <a href="/help?topicId=G200952510">Guide to Kindle Content Quality</a>. We reserve the right to change the <a href="/help?topicId=G200652170">categories</a> of a book at any time to ensure a positive customer experience.
<br><br>
<hr>
	<a name="publicdomain"></a>
<h3>Public domain content</h3>
We allow content that is in the public domain and no longer under copyright. However, to provide a better customer experience, we won’t allow undifferentiated versions of public domain titles if a free version is available in our store (as outlined in our policies for <a href="/help?topicId=G200743940">Publishing Public Domain Content</a>). We may ask publishers to provide proof that the content is in the public domain.<p> <br>
</p><hr><br><a name="Score and lyrics"></a>
<h3>Score and lyrics for songs managed by copyright management companies (Japan Only)</h3> Content containing scores and lyrics from songs managed by copyright management companies, including JASRAC, cannot be published on the Kindle Store.<p><br></p><hr>
	<a name="report"></a>
<h3>Report violations</h3>
If you believe a book violates our guidelines, please <a href="/help?topicId=G200652490">report it</a>.
<br><br>
Guidelines for other categories of products can be found here:
<br><br>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/external/200164670" target="_blank">Offensive and Controversial Materials</a>
</li><li><a href="https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=14279631" target="_blank">Community Guidelines</a>
</li><li><a href="https://aws.amazon.com/aup/" target="_blank">Amazon Web Services</a>

</li><li><a href="https://www.amazonregistry.com/legaldocs?docId=acceptableusepolicy" target="_blank">Amazon Registry</a>
</li></ul>

         <div class="a-section a-spacing-large">
            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Create a Paperback Cover
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               <div>
This resource covers the formatting requirements you’ll need to create a paperback cover yourself, using your chosen design software. For simple cover designs that meet KDP’s specifications, you can try our <a href="/help?topicId=G201113520">Cover Creator</a> tool.
<br>
<br>
Your cover must be a <b>single PDF</b> file that includes the back cover, spine, and front cover as one image.<br>
<br>
<b>Note:</b> To include spine text, your book must have at least 79 pages. If your manuscript is less than 79 pages, and spine text is included on the cover, the cover will be rejected and require adjustment before your book can go live. To calculate the size of your spine, based on your book’s page count, see the formula below, or try our <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/cover-calculator">cover calculator and template generator</a>. If you’re using <a href="/help?topicId=G201113520">Cover Creator</a>, the minimum page count for spine text is 80 pages.<br>
<br>
You have two cover finish options: glossy and matte. Learn more about <a href="/help?topicId=G201834180">print options</a>.
<br><br>
<div class="video-wrap">
<iframe frameborder="1" height="281" width="500" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/QZj3MKxDB8A?&theme=dark&autohide=2&showinfo=0&rel=0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen">
</iframe>
</div>
<b>Recorded webinar: Creative Cover Solutions</b>
<br><br>
<p></p>
<div class="a-span4">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<h3>Contents</h3>
<hr>
<ul>
<li><a href="#type_size">Supported file types and sizes</a>
</li><li><a href="#size">Setting your cover size</a>
<ul><li><a href="#spinemeasurement">Finding your spine measurement</a></li>
<li><a href="#spinetext">Spine text</a></li></ul>
</li><li><a href="#background">Formatting your cover background</a>
</li><li><a href="#images">Adding images</a>
</li><li><a href="#text">Adding text</a>
</li><li><a href="#barcode">Barcode size and placement</a>
</li><li><a href="#color">Color requirements</a>
</li><li><a href="#check">Pre-publication checklist</a>
</li><li><a href="#update">Update an existing cover</a></li></ul></div></div></div>
<hr>
<a name="type_size"></a>
<h3>
Supported file types and size limits
</h3>
<ul>
<li><b>File type.</b> Your cover must be a single PDF file that includes the back cover, spine, and front cover as one image.
</li><li><b>File size.</b> Cover files larger than 650MB won't convert. We recommend a file size of 40MB or less because large files can slow down printing.</li></ul>
<hr>
<a name="size"></a>
<h3>
Setting your cover size
</h3>
Your cover needs to be sized with bleed in order to meet our quality standards. Bleed is a printing term that refers to when printed items on a page, such as images or backgrounds, reach all the way to the edge of the page. To size your cover file with bleed, add 0.125" (3.2 mm) to the top, bottom, and outside edges of your cover.<br>
<br>
Our templates make it easier to create a print-ready paperback cover with programs that can open a PNG or PDF file and save a PDF file. <br>
<br>
If you want to set up your file yourself, try our <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/cover-calculator">cover calculator and template generator</a>. After you enter your ink and paper choices, trim size, and page count, the calculator will generate a layout like this:<br>
<br><br>
<img height="577" width="800" src="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindle-publication/EN/pback_temp_output.png"><br><br>
<ol>
<li><b>Full cover.</b> Total width and height of the cover file, including front, back, spine, and wrap.</li>
<li><b>Front cover.</b> Width and height of the visible cover area after it's printed. It's the same for the back cover too.</li>
<li><b>Safe area.</b> Place all text and images within this area, so they don’t shift to the front or back cover during printing.</li>
<li><b>Bleed.</b> Setting you bleed properly ensures printed objects reach all the way to the edge of the page. Accounting for bleed is important, because it prevents a white border from appearing at the edge of the page when the book is trimmed.</li>
<li><b>Margin.</b> Don't place text or images in this area, unless they're intended to wrap to the inside cover.</li>
<li><b>Spine.</b> The outside edge of the book where the pages are gathered and bound. Your book must have a minimum page count of 79 pages to include text on the spine.</li>
<li><b>Spine safe area.</b> Place all spine text and images within this area, so they don't shift to the front or back cover during printing.</li>
<li><b>Spine margin.</b> Don't place text or images in this spine area because they could shift to the front or back cover during printing.</li>
<li><b>Barcode margin.</b> This area ensures that the barcode doesn't shift during printing and scans properly.</li></ol><br>
<b>Note</b>: For Right to Left content, the <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/cover-calculator">cover calculator and template generator</a> will generate a layout with the front cover placed to the left of the spine and the back cover to the right of the spine. The barcode will be placed at the lower left-hand corner of your book’s back cover.</div><div><br> 
<a name="spinemeasurement"></a><h4>Finding your spine measurement</h4><br>
To format your paperback cover, you’ll first need to calculate the spine measurements.<br>
<br>
Insert the spine measurements, selected trim size width and height, and the 0.125" (3.2 mm) bleed requirement into the following equations to find your cover size:<br>
<br><ul>
<li>Cover Width = Bleed + Back Cover Width + Spine Width + Front Cover Width + Bleed</li>
<li>Cover Height = Bleed + Trim Height + Bleed</li>
</ul><br> 
<b>Spine measurements for black and white books</b><br>
<br><ul><li>White paper: page count x 0.002252" (0.0572 mm)</li>
<li>Cream paper: page count x 0.0025" (0.0635 mm)</li></ul>
<br>
<b>Spine measurements for color books</b><br>
<ul>
<li>Premium Color paper: page count x 0.002347" (0.0596 mm)</li>
<li>Standard Color paper: page count x 0.002252" (0.0572 mm)</li>
</ul>
<br>
<br><a name="spinetext"></a>
<h4>Spine text</h4><br>
We only print spine text on books with more than 79 pages. Text on larger spines must be sized to fit the spine, with at least 0.0625" (1.6 mm) of space between the text and the edge of the spine. Every book varies slightly when bound. Allow for 0.0625" (1.6 mm) variance on either side of the fold lines for your cover.<br>
<br>
<hr>
<a name="background"></a>
<h3>
Formatting your cover background
</h3><br><br>
<ul>
<li><b>Bleed.</b> All covers have bleed. If you want to add a background (e.g. color or image), make sure it extends 0.125" (3.2 mm) beyond the final trim line on all outside edges. All books are trimmed to size, and to ensure that the background fills the page, it needs to extend 0.125" (3.2 mm) past where the book will be trimmed on the top, bottom, and outside edges. This will prevent a white border from appearing at the edge when your book is trimmed.<br>
</li><li><b>Illegible text.</b> When choosing a background, consider how much it contrasts with the text. If the colors are too similar, the text might blend into the background and be hard to read.<br>
</li><li><b>Borders.</b> We don't recommend borders because we must allow for a 0.125" (3.2 mm) production variance that may trim the border or cause it to appear uneven. If your file includes borders, they should cover at least 0.25" (6.4 mm) inside the trim line. If you include a white border, it must meet our minimum border width or we may reject your file.</li></ul>
<br>
Shifting of the spine up to 0.0125" (3.2mm) in either direction is within acceptable print variance. If the shift is greater, the copy is considered defective. We don’t recommend hard edges on the spine due to the known 0.0125" (3.2mm) shift variance, as hard edges make this shift more apparent.
<p></p><br>
<hr>
<a></a>
<h3>
Adding images
</h3><br><br>
<ul>
<li><b>Bleed.</b> When adding images, make sure they extend 0.125" (3.2 mm) beyond the final trim line on all edges. This will prevent a white border from appearing at the edge when your book is trimmed.
</li><li><b>Image color, size, and quality.</b> Images should be in CMYK color to ensure your cover looks good in print. All images should be sized at 100%, flattened to one layer, and placed in your document at a minimum resolution of 300 DPI (dots per inch). Learn more about <a href="/help?topicId=G202169030">high-resolution images</a>.</li></ul>
<br>
<hr>
<a name="text"></a>
<h3>
Adding text</h3></div><div><h3> 
</h3><ul>
<li><b>Front and back cover text.</b> When adding text, make sure it's at least 0.125" (3.2 mm) inside the trim lines. Also, no front or back cover text should extend into the spine area.
</li><li><b>Spine text.</b> Your book must have at least 79 pages to add spine text. If your book has fewer than 79 pages, don’t add spine text. Also, spine text needs at least 0.0625" (1.6 mm) on either side so the text doesn't wrap onto the front or back cover.
</li><li><b>Book details.</b> As you add text to your cover, make sure it exactly matches the book details (e.g., title, author name, edition, ISBN) entered during title setup. Note that if you’re publishing a <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/GGE5T76TWKA85DJM">low-content book</a> using the <b>Publish without an ISBN</b> option, you do not need to add ISBN information on your cover. 
</li><li><b>Font size and color.</b> Text should be at least 7-point font so it's large enough for customers to read. Also, make sure the text doesn't blend into the background. This may happen if the text and background colors are too similar.</li></ul>
<br>
<iframe frameborder="0" height="315" width="560" allowfullscreen="" title="YouTube video player" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/EykFY2u7X-k"></iframe><br>
<b>Video: Illegible Text</b>
<br><br>
<hr>
<a name="barcode"></a>
<h3>Barcode size and placement</h3>
You can upload a cover with or without a barcode. If you choose not to provide your own barcode, we'll automatically place one on your back cover. Learn more about <a href="/help?topicId=G5HDYGP4BXLX4RUW">barcodes.</a>
<br><br>
<hr>
<a name="color"></a>
<h3>
Color requirements</h3></div><div><h3> 
</h3><ul>
<li><b>Color profiles.</b> Color management added to an image or file. We don't recommend including color profiles in your file. Color profiles can produce unexpected results. They are automatically removed before publishing.
</li><li><b>Spot colors.</b> Color generated from ink chosen from a color system (such as Pantone Matching System). Spot colors are used in offset printing and aren't compatible with KDP's print-on-demand model, so please don't include spot colors in your files. We recommend converting spot colors to CMYK.
</li><li><b>Color spaces.</b> Describes color numerically, such as RGB (digital cameras and computer monitors), CMYK (full-color printing), and grayscale (black and white printing). We don't recommend using multiple color spaces in a file because it can cause color variance and unexpected results when your book is printed.
</li><li><b>Color Variance.</b> With our print on demand model, we have acceptable levels of color tolerance. Most color variance happens as a result of environmental and mechanical factors. We always strive for the best quality when printing your title. Color variance occurs for many reasons that are not related to your file, however, taking all the steps you can to perfect your file will reduce the chances of it occurring.</li></ul>
<br>
<hr>
<a name="check"></a>
<h3>
Pre-publication checklist
</h3> </div><div><br></div><div>Before you upload your file to KDP, make sure you:
<br><br>
<ol>
<li><b>Save as a PDF.</b> Your cover must be a single PDF that includes the back cover, spine, and front cover as one image.</li>
<li><b>Flatten all transparencies.</b> These can cause the file to print with missing or distorted content. Consult your software's documentation to learn how.</li>
<li><b>Embed your fonts.</b> Consult your software's documentation to learn how.</li>
<li><b>Remove crop marks, color bars, template text.</b> Crop marks are lines showing where pages should be trimmed. Color bars are strips with a series of patches used to ensure color balance during printing. Also, remove any template text, PDF creation guides, or software references.</li>
<li><b>Ensure your cover image meets the minimum resolution</b> of 300 DPI (dots per inch).</li>
<li><b>Optimize PDFs.</b> Optimization is useful to reduce your file size, allowing for higher performance when transferring, uploading, viewing, and printing the files.</li>
<li><b>Remove file security.</b> Locked or encrypted files will fail review.</li>
<li><b>Check for missing or blank pages.</b> Manuscripts with missing pages, or excessive blank pages will be rejected.</li>
</ol>
<p></p><div><br></div>
Want to preview your book before making it available to customers? <a href="/help?topicId=G202131440">Order a proof copy</a>.
<br><br>
<hr>
<a name="update"></a>
<h3>
Update an existing cover
</h3> </div><div><br></div><div>To update your cover, go to your <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/bookshelf">Bookshelf</a> and <a href="/help?topicId=G200965970">follow these instructions</a>.</div>

            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Print Options
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               <div><div><div>Before you upload your manuscript and cover to KDP, you'll choose how you'd like to print your book. 
<br><br>
Visit <a href="/help?topicId=G201834340">Paperback Printing Cost</a> for details about how we calculate printing cost for paperbacks. For hardcover printing costs, visit <a href="/help?topicId=GHT976ZKSKUXBB6H">Hardcover Printing Cost</a>.<br><br><hr>
<div class="a-span4">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<h3>Contents</h3>
<hr>
<ul>

<a name="ink_paper"></a>
<h3>Ink and paper type</h3>

<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<b>New paper type available:</b> Groundwood paper is now available for paperback books with black and white interiors. <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G99WKT9FARBGHBJF">Learn more about groundwood paper</a>.
</div></div>
<br>

You can choose between these ink and paper options:

<br><br>

Black ink books can be printed on cream, white, or groundwood paper. Books with color ink are printed on white paper, which shows a higher contrast for images and graphics.

</div><div>
<hr>
<a name="selectprintoptions"></a>
<h3>Choose ink and paper type</h3>
<ol>
<li>Go to your <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/bookshelf">KDP Bookshelf</a>.</li>
<li>Click the ellipsis button ("…") next to the book you want to continue setup for</li>
<li>Choose <b>Edit paperback content</b> or <b>Edit hardcover content</b>.</li>
<li>Scroll to <b>Print Options</b> and choose your ink and paper type</li>
<li>Review and complete prompted checks on page</li>
<li>Select <b>Save and Continue</b>. This will take you to the <b>Rights & Pricing</b> page.</li>
<li>Click the <b>Publish</b> button at the bottom of the page to submit for publishing.</li>
</ol>

<p><b>Important:</b> When choosing your ink and paper type,</p>

<ul>
<li>Choose a <a href="/help?topicId=GX56BFPW4BKNPGFW">color ink option</a> if any images in your book are supposed to print in color. For paperbacks, you can choose between <b>premium color</b> and <b>standard color</b>. Standard color ink is not available for hardcover.</li>
<li>If your book is already published, the <a href="/help?topicId=G200736410#can_update_after_publishing">ink and paper type are locked</a> after publication due to ISBN requirements. After publication, you can't change your ink type between Standard color, Premium color, and black-and-white.</li>
<li>Set up a separate book on your <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/bookshelf">KDP Bookshelf</a> if you have a black-and-white and color version of your book.</li>
<li>We recommend ordering a proof of your book before publication to make sure selected ink and paper type fits your needs.</li>
<li>Remember that the cost for books printed in color is higher.</li>
<li>For groundwood paper, printing costs are approximately 5% lower per page compared to cream and white paper.</li>
</ul>

<p><b>Note:</b> Standard color distribution for right-to-left (RTL) paperbacks is limited to Amazon.co.jp.</p>
<br>
<a name="switching_paper"></a>
<h4>Switching paper types after publication</h4>

<p>If your paperback uses black and white ink, you can switch between certain paper types after publishing:</p>

<ul>
<li>Cream ↔ White</li>
<li>Cream ↔ Groundwood</li>
<li>White ↔ Groundwood</li>
</ul>

<p>Before switching, review your cover in the Print Previewer to ensure it displays correctly. Depending on your book's page count, you may need to upload a new cover file. Updates typically take up to 72 hours to appear. Learn more about our <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G202173620">publishing timelines</a>. Paper type switching is not available for titles using premium color or standard color ink.</p>

</a><a name="trim"></a>
<h3>Trim size</h3>
You can choose from a variety of trim sizes (check the table below for a list of common trim sizes, as well as minimum and maximum page count by size).<br>
<br>
The most common trim size for books in the U.S. is 6" x 9" (152.4 x 228.6 mm) and is a regular trim size. When setting up your book, this is the default in the "Print Options" section of the Content tab. If you want a different trim size, click <b>Select a different size</b>.
<br><br>
There are different printing costs for regular and large trim size books. A large trim size is either more than 6.12 inches (155.5 mm) in width or more than 9 inches (228.6 mm) in height.
<br><br>	
For paperbacks, you can also enter your own custom trim size. Width must be within 4"-8.5" (10.16-21.59 cm). Height must be within 6"-11.69" (15.24-29.69 cm). <br>

<a name="finish"></a>
<h3>Cover finish</h3>
Our covers are printed on 80 pound (220 GSM) white paper stock with either glossy or matte finish:
<br><br>
<ul>
<li><b>Glossy</b> finish is shiny. It makes black covers darker and artwork more striking. It's typical for textbooks, children's books, and nonfiction.</li>
<li><b>Matte</b> finish has minimal sheen and a subtle, polished look. It's typical for novels and other fiction.</li>
</ul>
<br>
<b>Note:</b> Hardcover books are printed as case laminate. For more information, visit <a href="/help?topicId=GKZVNAAFYWVKZWL8">Hardcover Print Elements</a>.<br>
<br><hr><br>
<a name="environmental"></a>
<h3>Environmental consciousness</h3>
<p>Environmental consciousness is important to us. As a manufacture-on-demand company, we produce units as they're ordered, which reduces excess production. We also maintain a commitment to recycling waste materials resulting from the printing process and from daily office operations, and we will continue to review our practices to ensure we are doing our part to protect the environment.</p>
<br><br>
<p>For information on EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), visit <a href="/help?topicId=GRWEDYN53XPNMFPN">EU Deforestation Regulation Compliance.</a></p>

            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Paperback Submission Guidelines
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               These guidelines are for <b>designers</b> of paperbacks with full-color covers, with any interior type.

<p>For help formatting your paperback manuscript, see our guides for <a href="/help?topicId=G202145400">Microsoft Word for Windows</a>, <a href="/help?topicId=GLRF8JDXY5LPE3TX">Microsoft Word for Mac</a> and <a href="/help?topicId=G3TQWMMGK8528NDZ">Pages for Mac</a>. You can also try our <a href="https://www.amazon.com/Kindle-Create/b?ie=UTF8&node=18292298011">Kindle Create</a> tool to format your paperback interiors.</p>

<div class="a-span4">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<h3>Contents</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="#limit">New title creation and submission limits</a></li>
<li><a href="#fileguide">File guidelines</a></li>
<li><a href="#coverspec">Cover specifications</a>
	<ul>
	<li><a href="#covercalc">Calculating cover size</a></li>
	<li><a href="#coverformat">Cover formatting</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinebw">Spine measurements for black and white books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinegw">Spine measurements for groundwood books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinecolor">Spine measurements for color books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinetext">Spine text</a></li>
	<li><a href="#barcode">Barcodes</a></li>
	</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="#intspec">Interior specifications</a></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3 id="limit">New title creation and submission limits</h3>
<p>To help promote a positive experience for all authors and readers, we limit how many new titles per format you can create and how many you can submit for publication each week. Both limits apply separately to each book format and reset every Sunday at 12:00 AM Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). For full details, visit <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G202172740">Create a Book</a>.

</p><hr>

<h3 id="fileguide">File guidelines</h3>

<h4 id="filems">Manuscript</h4>
<ul>
<li><b>Bleed:</b> If your book has images or elements that bleed to the edges of your pages, you must upload your manuscript as a PDF.</li>
<li><b>No Bleed:</b> If your book does not contain bleed, you can upload your manuscript as a PDF, DOC, DOCX, RTF, HTML, or TXT file. KDP will automatically convert these file types to PDF prior to publishing/printing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="filecover">Cover</h4>
<p>You can create your book cover using KDP's <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G201113520">Cover Creator</a> tool or submit your book cover in a PDF. (Cover Creator accepts JPG, PNG, and GIF file formats.)</p>

<h4 id="filespec">File specifications</h4>
<ul>
<li>Ensure file size is not more than 650MB.</li>
<li>File names for cover and interior files must not contain emoji characters or other unsupported special characters.</li>
<li>Embed all fonts and images in your native file prior to submission.</li>
<li>Flatten transparent objects and layers in the native file before publishing.</li>
<li>Submitted files should not contain crop marks, trim marks, bookmarks, comments, invisible objects, annotations, placeholder text, or metadata.</li>
<li>All images (both cover and manuscript) should be at least 300 DPI.</li>
<li>Optimize PDFs. Optimization is useful to reduce your file size, allowing for higher performance when transferring, uploading, viewing, and printing the files.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="filefail">Common points of failure</h4>
<ul>
<li>Not flattening transparent objects and/or layers in the native file</li>
<li>Locked or encrypted files</li>
<li>File names containing emoji or unsupported special characters</li>
<li>Files with crop marks, trim marks, bookmarks, comments, invisible objects, annotations, placeholder text, or metadata</li>
<li>Missing pages</li>
<li>Excessive blank pages</li>
<li>Title missing on the front cover</li>
<li>Barcode missing</li>
<li>Incorrect pagination</li>
<li>PDF creation logos or watermarks</li>
</ul>

<hr>

<h3 id="coverspec">Cover specifications</h3>

<h4 id="covercalc">Calculating cover size</h4>
<p>To format your paperback cover, you'll first need to calculate the spine measurements (<a href="#spinebw">black and white books</a>, <a href="#spinegw">groundwood books</a>, <a href="#spinecolor">color books</a>).</p>
<p>Insert the spine measurements, selected trim size width and height, and the 0.125" (3.2 mm) bleed requirement into the following equations to find your cover size:</p>
<ul>
<li>Cover Width = Bleed + Back Cover Width + Spine Width + Front Cover Width + Bleed</li>
<li>Cover Height = Bleed + Trim Height + Bleed</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="coverformat">Cover formatting</h4>
<ul>
<li>Covers should be one continuous image centered left to right on the spine.</li>
<li>Flatten all layers in the native file.</li>
<li>Bleed of 0.125" (3.2 mm) is required on all sides. Bleed at the bottom of the page cannot exceed 0.125" (3.2 mm).</li>
<li>Any content you don't intend to be trimmed off should be a minimum of 0.25" (6.4 mm) from the outside cover edge.</li>
<li>Embed all fonts on the cover in the native program before publishing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinebw">Spine measurements for black and white books</h4>
<ul>
<li>White paper: page count x 0.002252" (0.0572 mm)</li>
<li>Cream paper: page count x 0.0025" (0.0635 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinegw">Spine measurements for groundwood books</h4>
<ul>
<li>Groundwood paper: page count x 0.00235" (0.0596 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinecolor">Spine measurements for color books</h4>
<ul>
<li>Color paper: page count x 0.002347" (0.0596 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinetext">Spine text</h4>
<p>We only print spine text on books with more than 79 pages. Text on larger spines must be sized to fit the spine, with at least 0.0625" (1.6 mm) of space between the text and the edge of the spine. Every book varies slightly when bound. Allow for 0.0625" (1.6 mm) variance on either side of the fold lines for your cover.</p>

<h4 id="barcode">Barcodes</h4>
<p>You can upload a cover with or without a barcode. If you choose not to provide your own barcode, we'll automatically place one on your back cover. Learn more about <a href="/help?topicId=G5HDYGP4BXLX4RUW">barcodes</a>.</p>

<hr>

<h3 id="intspec">Interior specifications</h3>

<h4 id="pagespread">Page spreads</h4>
<p>We require single page files (as opposed to spreads or 2-up files).</p>

<h4 id="pagesize">Page size</h4>

<h5 id="nobleed">No bleed</h5>
<p>Set the page size to your selected trim size (width by height).</p>

<h5 id="bleed">Interior full bleed</h5>
<ul>
<li>If you want your images to bleed to the edges of your pages, extend them 0.125" (3.2 mm) beyond the final trim size from the top, bottom, and outer edges of your manuscript.</li>
<li>Format your PDF manuscript at 0.25" (6.4 mm) higher and 0.125" (3.2 mm) wider than your selected trim size in order to print the full bleed area.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="font">Font</h4>
<ul>
<li>Minimum font size: 7 points</li>
<li>All fonts in the interior files should be embedded in the native program before publishing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="imgres">Image resolution</h4>
<p>Minimum resolution of 300 DPI. There is no set maximum DPI for images, however, images with excessively high resolutions may result in files timing out during processing, or may cause manufacturing delays. We recommend a maximum resolution of 600 DPI, to keep your total file size under 650MB.</p>

<h4 id="pag">Pagination</h4>
<ul>
<li>Order all page numbers sequentially, with even numbers on left pages and odd numbers on the right for the left to right content, and with even numbers on right pages and odd numbers on the left for the right to left content.</li>
<li>You can use Roman numerals to indicate the beginning of the manuscript, and then continue with standard page numbering.</li>
<li>You may continue page numbering from a previous book in a subsequent volume of a series as long as the series name and volume number are clearly labeled.</li>
<li>We allow scanned content with sequential original page numbering clearly visible in the footer of the manuscript file.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="pagcount">Page count</h4>
<p>We'll calculate your page count based on your manuscript file, rounding up to an even number if necessary. The minimum page count is 24 pages, and the maximum page count depends on ink, paper, and trim size options.</p>

            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Paperback Submission Guidelines
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               These guidelines are for <b>designers</b> of paperbacks with full-color covers, with any interior type.

<p>For help formatting your paperback manuscript, see our guides for <a href="/help?topicId=G202145400">Microsoft Word for Windows</a>, <a href="/help?topicId=GLRF8JDXY5LPE3TX">Microsoft Word for Mac</a> and <a href="/help?topicId=G3TQWMMGK8528NDZ">Pages for Mac</a>. You can also try our <a href="https://www.amazon.com/Kindle-Create/b?ie=UTF8&node=18292298011">Kindle Create</a> tool to format your paperback interiors.</p>

<div class="a-span4">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<h3>Contents</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="#limit">New title creation and submission limits</a></li>
<li><a href="#fileguide">File guidelines</a></li>
<li><a href="#coverspec">Cover specifications</a>
	<ul>
	<li><a href="#covercalc">Calculating cover size</a></li>
	<li><a href="#coverformat">Cover formatting</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinebw">Spine measurements for black and white books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinegw">Spine measurements for groundwood books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinecolor">Spine measurements for color books</a></li>
	<li><a href="#spinetext">Spine text</a></li>
	<li><a href="#barcode">Barcodes</a></li>
	</ul>
</li>

</ul>
</div>

<hr>

<h3 id="limit">New title creation and submission limits</h3>
<p>To help promote a positive experience for all authors and readers, we limit how many new titles per format you can create and how many you can submit for publication each week. Both limits apply separately to each book format and reset every Sunday at 12:00 AM Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). For full details, visit <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G202172740">Create a Book</a>.

</p><hr>

<h3 id="fileguide">File guidelines</h3>

<h4 id="filems">Manuscript</h4>
<ul>
<li><b>Bleed:</b> If your book has images or elements that bleed to the edges of your pages, you must upload your manuscript as a PDF.</li>
<li><b>No Bleed:</b> If your book does not contain bleed, you can upload your manuscript as a PDF, DOC, DOCX, RTF, HTML, or TXT file. KDP will automatically convert these file types to PDF prior to publishing/printing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="filecover">Cover</h4>
<p>You can create your book cover using KDP's <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G201113520">Cover Creator</a> tool or submit your book cover in a PDF. (Cover Creator accepts JPG, PNG, and GIF file formats.)</p>

<h4 id="filespec">File specifications</h4>
<ul>
<li>Ensure file size is not more than 650MB.</li>
<li>File names for cover and interior files must not contain emoji characters or other unsupported special characters.</li>
<li>Embed all fonts and images in your native file prior to submission.</li>
<li>Flatten transparent objects and layers in the native file before publishing.</li>
<li>Submitted files should not contain crop marks, trim marks, bookmarks, comments, invisible objects, annotations, placeholder text, or metadata.</li>
<li>All images (both cover and manuscript) should be at least 300 DPI.</li>
<li>Optimize PDFs. Optimization is useful to reduce your file size, allowing for higher performance when transferring, uploading, viewing, and printing the files.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="filefail">Common points of failure</h4>
<ul>
<li>Not flattening transparent objects and/or layers in the native file</li>
<li>Locked or encrypted files</li>
<li>File names containing emoji or unsupported special characters</li>
<li>Files with crop marks, trim marks, bookmarks, comments, invisible objects, annotations, placeholder text, or metadata</li>
<li>Missing pages</li>
<li>Excessive blank pages</li>
<li>Title missing on the front cover</li>
<li>Barcode missing</li>
<li>Incorrect pagination</li>
<li>PDF creation logos or watermarks</li>
</ul>

<hr>

<h3 id="coverspec">Cover specifications</h3>

<h4 id="covercalc">Calculating cover size</h4>
<p>To format your paperback cover, you'll first need to calculate the spine measurements (<a href="#spinebw">black and white books</a>, <a href="#spinegw">groundwood books</a>, <a href="#spinecolor">color books</a>).</p>
<p>Insert the spine measurements, selected trim size width and height, and the 0.125" (3.2 mm) bleed requirement into the following equations to find your cover size:</p>
<ul>
<li>Cover Width = Bleed + Back Cover Width + Spine Width + Front Cover Width + Bleed</li>
<li>Cover Height = Bleed + Trim Height + Bleed</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="coverformat">Cover formatting</h4>
<ul>
<li>Covers should be one continuous image centered left to right on the spine.</li>
<li>Flatten all layers in the native file.</li>
<li>Bleed of 0.125" (3.2 mm) is required on all sides. Bleed at the bottom of the page cannot exceed 0.125" (3.2 mm).</li>
<li>Any content you don't intend to be trimmed off should be a minimum of 0.25" (6.4 mm) from the outside cover edge.</li>
<li>Embed all fonts on the cover in the native program before publishing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinebw">Spine measurements for black and white books</h4>
<ul>
<li>White paper: page count x 0.002252" (0.0572 mm)</li>
<li>Cream paper: page count x 0.0025" (0.0635 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinegw">Spine measurements for groundwood books</h4>
<ul>
<li>Groundwood paper: page count x 0.00235" (0.0596 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinecolor">Spine measurements for color books</h4>
<ul>
<li>Color paper: page count x 0.002347" (0.0596 mm)</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="spinetext">Spine text</h4>
<p>We only print spine text on books with more than 79 pages. Text on larger spines must be sized to fit the spine, with at least 0.0625" (1.6 mm) of space between the text and the edge of the spine. Every book varies slightly when bound. Allow for 0.0625" (1.6 mm) variance on either side of the fold lines for your cover.</p>

<h4 id="barcode">Barcodes</h4>
<p>You can upload a cover with or without a barcode. If you choose not to provide your own barcode, we'll automatically place one on your back cover. Learn more about <a href="/help?topicId=G5HDYGP4BXLX4RUW">barcodes</a>.</p>

<hr>

<h3 id="intspec">Interior specifications</h3>

<h4 id="pagespread">Page spreads</h4>
<p>We require single page files (as opposed to spreads or 2-up files).</p>

<h4 id="pagesize">Page size</h4>

<h5 id="nobleed">No bleed</h5>
<p>Set the page size to your selected trim size (width by height).</p>

<h5 id="bleed">Interior full bleed</h5>
<ul>
<li>If you want your images to bleed to the edges of your pages, extend them 0.125" (3.2 mm) beyond the final trim size from the top, bottom, and outer edges of your manuscript.</li>
<li>Format your PDF manuscript at 0.25" (6.4 mm) higher and 0.125" (3.2 mm) wider than your selected trim size in order to print the full bleed area.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="font">Font</h4>
<ul>
<li>Minimum font size: 7 points</li>
<li>All fonts in the interior files should be embedded in the native program before publishing.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="imgres">Image resolution</h4>
<p>Minimum resolution of 300 DPI. There is no set maximum DPI for images, however, images with excessively high resolutions may result in files timing out during processing, or may cause manufacturing delays. We recommend a maximum resolution of 600 DPI, to keep your total file size under 650MB.</p>

<h4 id="pag">Pagination</h4>
<ul>
<li>Order all page numbers sequentially, with even numbers on left pages and odd numbers on the right for the left to right content, and with even numbers on right pages and odd numbers on the left for the right to left content.</li>
<li>You can use Roman numerals to indicate the beginning of the manuscript, and then continue with standard page numbering.</li>
<li>You may continue page numbering from a previous book in a subsequent volume of a series as long as the series name and volume number are clearly labeled.</li>
<li>We allow scanned content with sequential original page numbering clearly visible in the footer of the manuscript file.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="pagcount">Page count</h4>
<p>We'll calculate your page count based on your manuscript file, rounding up to an even number if necessary. The minimum page count is 24 pages, and the maximum page count depends on ink, paper, and trim size options.</p>

<style type="text/css">
html {
   overflow-y: scroll;
}

body {
   padding: 0;
   margin: 0;
   -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
   font: 13px/1.231 arial, helvetica, clean, sans-serif;
}

body.warn-page {
   background: #ffffcc;
}

#page-container {
   margin: 0;
   padding: 0;
   min-width: 1275px;
}

.kdp-top-header {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindlepubs/common/layouts/nav-bar-bg._V156427298_.png")
      repeat-x scroll 0 0 transparent;
   height: 29px;
}

.header-row {
   background-color: #F5F5F5;
   padding-top: 6px;
   padding-bottom: 3px;
}

.top-links {
   padding: 5px 20px;
   text-align: right;
}

.top-links a, .top-links .language-chooser, .header-item, .header-item .language-chooser {
   margin: 0 10px;
}

.kdp-delim {
   color: #CCCCCC;
}

.language-option {
   font-size: 11px;
}

.language-option a {
